result:
On load, the app asks the server who is signed in before it renders anything. `apps/react-vite/src/app/provider.tsx` wraps the whole tree in `AuthLoader`, which `configureAuth` from `react-query-auth` creates in `src/lib/auth.tsx`. Its `userFn` is `getUser`, which calls `GET /auth/me` through the shared Axios instance in `src/lib/api-client.ts`. While that request is pending, `AuthLoader` shows a full-screen spinner. Once it settles, the result is held as the `useUser()` query. Routes under `/app` are wrapped in `ProtectedRoute` (used in `src/app/router.tsx`), which checks `user.data`. If there is no user, it renders a `Navigate` to `/auth/login?redirectTo=<current path>` (built by `paths.auth.login.getHref` in `src/config/paths.ts`). The auth layout (`src/components/layouts/auth-layout.tsx`) and the login and register routes then send a signed-in user on to `redirectTo` or `/app`.

Every API call goes through the Axios instance in `src/lib/api-client.ts`. Its request interceptor sets `withCredentials = true` so the session cookie is sent. Its response interceptor is where a 401 is handled. For any error, it first shows an error toast with the server's `message`, or Axios's own message if there is none. If the status is 401, it sets `window.location.href` to the login page, so the browser does a full page load rather than a client-side route change. The error is then still rejected, so the calling query or mutation also sees it. Queries have `retry: false` in `src/lib/react-query.ts`, so a 401 is not retried.

The `redirectTo` handling in that 401 branch does not work as intended. It reads `searchParams` from a new, empty `URLSearchParams()`, so it always falls back to `window.location.pathname`. Any query string on the current page is lost, and the code never reads a `redirectTo` already in the URL. Because `/auth/login` is not excluded from the interceptor, a 401 from a sign-in attempt would also trigger this full-page redirect. I did not check the login endpoint's error status in the real API or the mock handlers, so treat that last point as a likely edge case rather than a confirmed bug.

I made no file changes.
